crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Brain Computer Interfaces
children.blurb: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read electrical or chemical signals from the nervous system and translate them into commands for a computer, a prosthetic, or a communication aid, and in some designs write information back into the brain through stimulation.

children.name: Early Signals of Dementia
children.blurb: Early signals of dementia refers to computational detection of subtle cognitive, behavioral, motor, or biomarker changes that may precede a clinical diagnosis.

children.name: Functional MRI Interpretation
children.blurb: Functional MRI interpretation uses AI to map brain activity from blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals, identify activation patterns tied to tasks or resting states, and support localization of language, motor, and memory functions before surgery.

children.name: Seizure Prediction
children.blurb: Seizure prediction is the use of machine learning to estimate the likelihood that a person with epilepsy will have a seizure within a short upcoming window, usually minutes to hours, based on physiological signals.

children.name: Cognitive Rehabilitation
children.blurb: Cognitive rehabilitation in this context covers AI systems that assess, train, and support recovery of cognitive functions such as attention, memory, executive function, and language after stroke, traumatic brain injury, or in neurodegenerative conditions.

sections.body: Neuroinformatics and the Brain is the part of The AI Physician that covers artificial intelligence applied to brain data and brain related care. It spans direct communication with neural signals, early signs of dementia, functional MRI interpretation, seizure prediction, and cognitive rehabilitation. In practice the work is mostly pattern recognition on large, noisy datasets such as electrophysiology, imaging, clinical notes, and behavioral scores. Brain computer interfaces use machine learning to decode intended movement or speech from neural activity, often through implanted or wearable sensors. Dementia research looks for subtle changes in speech, gait, imaging, or cognitive tests that may appear before a formal diagnosis. Functional MRI interpretation maps activity and connectivity, seizure prediction tries to forecast epileptic events from EEG or other signals, and cognitive rehabilitation uses adaptive software or stimulation to support attention, memory, or language.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: This site tracks 1000 medical AI models, and the neuroinformatics pages in this section belong to that broader medical set. Some narrow tasks are now reliable in research settings, including automated segmentation of brain images, detection of certain EEG patterns, and extraction of speech or gait features linked to cognitive decline. What is not solved is the jump from a good benchmark to dependable clinical use, because models often fail when scanners, patient populations, or recording protocols change. Brain computer interfaces have produced clear demonstrations of cursor control and speech decoding, yet long term signal stability, surgical risk, calibration time, and limited participant numbers keep them far from routine care. Dementia signal work remains probabilistic and cannot replace a clinical evaluation, functional MRI interpretation is complicated by site effects, motion, and weak causal inference, and seizure prediction still struggles with false alarms and uncertain lead time. Cognitive rehabilitation studies are small, heterogeneous, and unclear about whether gains transfer to daily life, and the honest limits across all five areas are data scarcity, bias, privacy, regulatory uncertainty, and a shortage of prospective trials that show patient benefit.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages in this section move from direct neural interfaces to population level signals and then to rehabilitation. Brain Computer Interfaces is the place to start for hardware, decoding methods, and the ethics of implanted or wearable systems. Early Signals of Dementia covers speech, gait, imaging, and cognitive test models that look for subtle decline before diagnosis. Functional MRI Interpretation explains how models read activity and connectivity, and why scanner and motion artifacts matter. Seizure Prediction focuses on EEG and other time series, detection versus forecasting, and the false alarm problem. Cognitive Rehabilitation looks at adaptive training, closed loop stimulation, and outcome measures after injury or illness.
